messages:
incident-bot: P0 Pager -> HelixSystems (tenant helix-452) dedicated pool eu-central-1 reporting >12% 5xx errors and elevated latency since 21:41 UTC. Routing to #incidents and helix oncall.

Sam (oncall): Picking this up. I see the spike in the inference-proxy metrics and pods restarting intermittently. Will reproduce against their pool.

Jess (PSM): Helix confirms their chat autocomplete and email-summarization flows are failing intermittently, ~15% errors. They've throttled non-critical traffic. No data leakage reported.

Omar (SRE): Triage notes from logs: runtime-returned 500 with "KV-index pressure: allocation refused" and proxy 502s when backend returned truncated frames. Errors correlate with requests that have long conversations + attachments.

Talia (eng-runtime): We rolled runtime 3.0.1 to dedicated fleets last night. There was a latent change to the KV index growth heuristic that could mis-handle some chunked tokenization. Checking tenant config: helix-452 uses model family "redwood-alpha" with auto-minor-updates enabled.

Kevin (SE): Helix's SLA requires minimal disruption; they prefer a non-rollback approach if we can do an opaque switch. They want to avoid client-side changes.

Sam (oncall): Immediate mitigation options: 1) switch Helix traffic to compact safe variant redwood-alpha-compact; 2) pin tenant to last-known-good model version and pause auto-updates; 3) increase per-tenant KV cache quota temporarily. Recommend option 1 first for speed.

Jess (PSM): Helix opted for safe-variant switch if it can be done <20m with no app changes.

Talia (eng-runtime): I can apply a tenant-level fallback rule. Plan: update routing to redwood-alpha-compact@v20250310-stable, pin=true, override-auto-updates=true, weight=100. Will run a small canary within the dedicated pool. Need control-plane go to push immediately.

Omar (SRE): Prior to the switch, capturing heap/KV histograms and thread dumps. Commands:
```
kubectl -n runtime logs -l tenant=helix-452 -f | sed -n '1,200p' > /tmp/helix-runtime-tail.log
/sbin/collect-heap -o /tmp/helix-heap-$(date +%s).hprof --pids $(pgrep runtime)
```
Saving to secure bucket for Helix's engineering team.

Sam (oncall): Assigning tasks: Talia perform routing change (5-10m), Omar collect dumps/logs (5m), Jess inform Helix (ETA 5m). I'll coordinate smoke tests.

Jess (PSM): Messaging Helix: "We're implementing a rapid safe-variant switch on your dedicated pool. No client changes required. ETA ~15m. We'll follow with logs and an RCA." Helix acknowledged: "Proceed."

incident-bot: Canary capacity check: eu-central-1 dedicated pool has sufficient spare headroom.

Talia (eng-runtime): Executing routing update:
```
redwoodctl tenant set-fallback --tenant helix-452 \\
  --variant redwood-alpha-compact@v20250310-stable --pin true --no-auto-update --weight 100
```
Update submitted to control plane, awaiting propagation.

Omar (SRE): Starting smoke tests against the tenant's staging queries and watching ingress errors.

incident-bot: Control plane reported propagation completed for tenant helix-452.

Sam (oncall): Running synthetic queries now. Latency looks stable, errors trending down.

Jess (PSM): Helix reports immediate improvement: errors down to ~1.8% and UX tests passing for quick flows. They thanked the team.

Talia (eng-runtime): Observability shows stabilized memory/KV metrics after variant switch. No pod restarts in last 8m. Collecting flamegraphs to root cause. Preliminary signal: the 3.0.1 heuristic allows indefinite KV growth for multi-attachment requests when tokenization produces many small segments. Compact variant reduces per-request KV footprint and avoids the pathological growth.

Omar (SRE): Heap and KV histograms captured and uploaded to Helix S3 with limited retention, plus a redacted runtime log bundle.

Talia (eng-runtime): Proposed follow-ups:
- hotfix runtime 3.0.2 to tighten KV-growth guards (owner: eng-runtime, ETA 48h)
- add per-tenant max-conversation-length enforcement and a preflight router to route pathological requests to compact variants (owner: infra+runtime, ETA 7d)
- provide Helix opt-in automated failover policy (owner: runtime, ETA 3d)

Sam (oncall): Draft failover policy idea:
```
policy {
  tenant: helix-452
  trigger: tenant_5xx_rate > 5% for 180s
  action: switch_variant("redwood-alpha-compact@v20250310-stable", pin=true)
  cooldown: 30m
}
```
Would require per-tenant 5xx metric emission.

Jess (PSM): Helix asked if we can make that automatic for their tenant. I confirmed it's possible as an opt-in. They want it enabled.

Talia (eng-runtime): Note: need infra to expose per-tenant 5xx SLI. Adding task: infra to emit tenant-level 5xx and kv-pressure metrics (ETA 48h).

Sam (oncall): Decision: manual safe-variant switch applied (done); pin for 30m; schedule hotfix and implement opt-in automated failover for Helix. Continue monitoring.

Jess (PSM): Helix requested a short post-incident summary and copies of the collected artifacts. I've arranged secure delivery and will follow up with the RCA and timeline for 3.0.2.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated by tenant variant switch. Severity downgraded to P1. Follow-ups created and owners assigned.

Sam (oncall): Handoff to overnight SRE (Omar) for monitoring. If 5xx >3% will page immediately.

Omar (SRE): Onwatch overnight. I've added a dashboard for per-tenant errors and KV pressure. Will escalate if trend reverses.

Jess (PSM): Thanks team. Helix: "Appreciate the quick response. We'll coordinate a longer maintenance window to validate the hotfix."

Sam (oncall): Closing live coordination thread. Will file incident ticket and postmortem doc with action items: runtime hotfix, infra metrics, tenant-level policy opt-in, artifact handoff. Tags: customer-impact, vpc, dedicated-pool, model-fallback, runtime-kvregress.
